title: sao.1: feed module skeleton + route registration
description:
What: Create crates/mail/src/feed.rs skeleton and register /feed/*path route in build_router().

Algorithm:
1. Create crates/mail/src/feed.rs with:
   a. A pub fn escape_xml(s: &str) -> String that replaces & → & FIRST, then < → <, > → >, " → ", ' → '
   b. A pub fn parse_feed_path(path: &str) -> Option<(&str, FeedFormat)> that:
      - Takes a path like 'comp.lang.rust.rss' or 'comp.lang.rust.atom'
      - Strips trailing .rss → FeedFormat::Rss or .atom → FeedFormat::Atom
      - Returns the group name portion (e.g. 'comp.lang.rust') and the format
      - Returns None if path doesn't end in .rss or .atom
   c. pub enum FeedFormat { Rss, Atom }
   d. A stub: pub async fn feed_handler(State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>, Path(path): Path<String>) -> impl IntoResponse { todo!() }

2. Add 'pub mod feed;' to crates/mail/src/lib.rs

3. In crates/mail/src/server.rs build_router():
   - Add to the public (non-auth) router: .route('/feed/*path', get(crate::feed::feed_handler))
   - The route must come BEFORE the CORS layer and be in the public section (no basic_auth_middleware)

Defensive programming:
- escape_xml must escape & FIRST to avoid double-escaping
- parse_feed_path must handle edge cases: just '.rss' (empty group name → return None), path with no dots, path ending in neither .rss nor .atom

Tests: unit tests for escape_xml (verify & is not double-escaped) and parse_feed_path (happy + edge cases).
Acceptance: cargo check passes; route is registered.
